## Summary

He measured which robustness checks actually discriminate real edges from junk, on data-mined strategies. The table (OCR-recovered):

| Check | Junk passed | Real edges passed | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MCPT** (Monte Carlo Permutation Test, Masters) | **1.4%** | **76%** | "The best single check. It tells real edges from luck well." |
| **Walk-Forward** | **0.2%** | **44%** | "Strict, but it is the only check that catches edges that stop working." |
| Monte Carlo Retest (SQX) | 15% | 63% | "Lets a lot of junk through. Useful at most as a cost stress at the end." |
| SPP (System Parameter Permutation) | 0–5% | 64% (2–45% range) | "Lets junk through and overlaps with Walk-Forward. Adds little." |
| Sequential Optimization | — | — | "Overlaps with Walk-Forward. Strict settings fail almost every edge, and loosening it lets junk in." |

Headline finding (his words): "Walk Forward and MCPT are the standouts. Parameter stability checks like sequential optimization and SPP added nothing when used alongside Walk Forward. They actually hurt the pipeline."

## Why it matters

- Directly actionable on our own stack: the MarginCall4 audit standard we set two days ago ([[2026-10-28-margincall4-overfitting-validation-dsr-pbo-walkforward]]) leans on DSR + PBO + walk-forward. Martin's calibration says the load-bearing checks are **WF + MCPT**, and that stacking extra parameter-stability checks on top of WF is not free — it can reject real edges. Third dmartin capture, all one program: [[2026-10-01-dmartin-hypothesis-first]] (research discipline) → [[2026-10-24-dmartin-deflated-sharpe-ratio]] (the DSR explainer) → this (which checks to actually run).
- The junk-passed column is the multiple-testing hygiene our TF-queue standards keep circling ([[2026-10-26-lucasjoly-thesis-ctafutures-trend-research]], [[2026-10-21-setupalpha-trend-system-robustness-tests]]): a check that passes 15% of junk strategies (MC Retest) isn't a validation, it's a vibe.
- **Skepticism gates:** single author, self-built test harness, no sample sizes / edge counts / data published in the tweet — the rates are his summary of his own research; "junk" and "real edge" are his labels (circularity risk he'd presumably address in the blog). WF passing only 44% of real edges cuts both ways: strict means false negatives are the price. OCR cells approximate until checked against full-res.
